sentences.reason: Title sentence; states the thesis as a conceptual claim. No external descriptive premise is added. Basis is reasoning.

Explains why the distinction matters to developers. 'Can make … look open' is a capability conditional, not an asserted fact about real actors. 'Important decisions happened before the user arrived' follows from the definition in p1s2. No external premise added. Basis is reasoning.
Section heading posed as a rhetorical question. No descriptive premise. Basis is reasoning.
Direct answer to the rhetorical question; 'not initially' qualifies the claim appropriately as definitional. No external premise. Basis is reasoning.

Transitional sentence extending the argument to defaults. No external premise. Basis is reasoning.

Provides an analytical characterisation of a default ('recommendation with momentum') with illustrative examples (preselected browser, first-listed provider, etc.) as conceptual instances, not asserted facts about named actors. Basis is reasoning.

Labeled reasoning, but introduces two external descriptive premises: (1) the behavioral claim that many users will not change a default, and (2) a causal explanation that non-switching is driven by attention cost, time cost, and confidence deficit. These are not derived from prior definitions; they assert facts about real user populations and causal mechanisms, constituting broad generalizations with no ledger support.

claims.claim: Many users who encounter a default setting will not change it.
claims.verification_question: Is there empirical evidence (e.g., studies on default persistence) showing that a substantial majority or large share of users leave defaults unchanged?

claims.claim: Users fail to change defaults primarily because doing so requires attention, time, and confidence that the alternative will work as well.
claims.evidence: changing it takes attention, time, and confidence that the alternative will work as well
claims.verification_question: What research or evidence identifies attention cost, time cost, and performance uncertainty as the principal reasons users do not change defaults?
